verdict.rationale: Mem0 documents per-memory deletion through its CLI and a per-memory expiration_date. Expiration only hides memories from search ('Nothing is deleted'), so it is not true retention-based deletion. Self-hosting gives users ownership of their data. missing for 10: retention policies that actually purge data, documented bulk or account-level deletion and its guarantees (e.g. hard delete, backups), independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can control data retention and deletion

citations.quote: The mem0 CLI lets you add, search, list, update, and delete memories directly from the terminal.
Set an expiration date on a Mem0 memory and it stops surfacing in search once that date passes. Nothing is deleted.
You own the stack, the data, and every component
